data.title: Dinari Launches Tokenized Anthropic Shares on First Day of Nasdaq Trading
data.description:
San Mateo, United States, November 19th, 2026, Chainwire

Following SpaceX and SK hynix, Dinari continues expanding access to major public market debuts through its custodial tokenization infrastructure.

Dinari, a global financial infrastructure company enabling the issuance, settlement, management and distribution of tokenized securities, today announced the launch of Anthropic dShares , making tokenized representations of Anthropic available to eligible investors in the United States and internationally on the company's first day of public trading on Nasdaq.

The launch follows Dinari's tokenization of other highly anticipated public listings this year, including SpaceX and SK hynix, reinforcing the company's ability to bring newly listed equities to global markets from their first day of trading.

Through Dinari's growing distribution network of financial institutions, brokerages, and fintech platforms, eligible investors can access ANT dShares across 92 jurisdictions. In the United States, brokerage services are offered only by Dinari Securities, LLC, Member FINRA/SIPC.

Some tokenized stock products provide exposure to price movement only. Dinari’s dShares are backed by corresponding securities held through licensed custodians. The custodial structure preserves the economic benefits and applicable shareholder rights associated with traditional securities, including dividends, and applicable corporate actions.

"Anthropic's IPO is another example of how tokenization can expand access to public markets without compromising the rights of traditional securities," said Gabriel Otte, CEO and Co-Founder of Dinari. "From SpaceX to Anthropic, we're demonstrating that tokenized equities can be available from the first day of trading, supported by the same underlying securities and established market infrastructure."

Through a single API integration, Dinari enables financial institutions and distribution partners to offer tokenized U.S. equities while supporting securities custody, issuance and redemption, corporate actions, and compliance.

For more information, visit dinari.com.

About Dinari

Dinari is a global financial infrastructure company enabling the issuance, settlement, management and distribution of tokenized securities. Its technology helps broker-dealers, financial institutions, asset managers and digital platforms add tokenized securities to their products and distribute them across the U.S. and 92 jurisdictions globally. Dinari pioneered the custodial model which preserves the rights and protections of the underlying securities while supporting faster settlement, stablecoin-based payments and new financial applications.

Disclaimer

Dinari Inc. is a technology company and is not a broker-dealer. In the United States, brokerage services are offered by Dinari Securities LLC, member FINRA/SIPC.

Check the background of Dinari Securities on FINRA’s BrokerCheck. An investor brochure describing BrokerCheck is available on request, or from FINRA at (800) 289-9999. Dinari Securities does not provide investment advice or recommendations and does not monitor your account; all orders are self-directed. SIPC protection does not cover market losses and does not cover dShares transferred to a self-custody wallet.

This material is for informational and educational purposes only and does not constitute investment advice or an offer to sell or solicitation of an offer to buy securities. Investing in IPO securities involves significant risk, including substantial price volatility, limited trading history, potential liquidity constraints, and the possibility of losing principal. IPO offering prices may differ materially from secondary-market trading prices.

All availability, trading functionality, and timing described above are subject to change. Investors should review Anthropic's SEC filings and applicable Dinari disclosures before making investment decisions.

For additional information, visit dinari.com/terms.

data.title: U.S. Treasury 10-Year TIPS Auction Pays Highest Yield in 24 Years
data.description:
By Paulo Trevisani

A U.S. Treasury auction of 10-year inflation-protected securities on Thursday cleared the highest yield in 24 years.

The Treasury sold $19 billion in 10-year TIPS paying a high yield of 2.903%, the highest since July 2002, when the high yield was 3.099%.

Thursday's auction was a reopening, while the one in July 2002 was a new issue.

The bid-to-cover ratio, a measure of demand for the securities, increased to 2.43 from 2.24 in the latest 10-year TIPS auction, held in September.

Indirect bidders, a group that includes foreign buyers, took $12.97 billion in competitive bids.

The auction happened as sticky inflation increased the chances of a steep rise in interest rates by the Federal Reserve.

Write to Paulo Trevisani at paulo.trevisani@wsj.com

data.title: Judge rejects New York Times' bid to block Trump's $15B defamation lawsuit
data.description:
A Florida judge ruled that President Donald Trump can proceed with a defamation lawsuit against the New York Times as the newspaper acted with “actual malice” in accusing the president of money laundering, tax fraud, tax evasion, and related criminal conduct.

Trump is suing The New York Times for $15B, alleging that its reporting tarnished his reputation with false stories of his business acumen heading into the 2024 presidential election.

The lawsuit also names Penguin Random House, the publisher of Lucky Loser: How Donald Trump Squandered His Father’s Fortune and Create the Illusion of Success.

U.S. District Judge Steven Merryday denied the newspaper’s effort to dismiss the case but threw out two other allegations and narrowed the scope of four others. In keeping the remaining claims, Merryday agreed with Trump that the NYT knew the statements made by its journalists were false or they acted “with reckless disregard for the truth” and failed to qualify its accusations of tax fraud from a “qualified source.”

“Knowing of the necessity for that opinion but failing to procure that opinion is a fine example of the purposeful avoidance of the truth,” Merryday said in his decision.

The New York Times has not yet responded to Seeking Alpha’s request for comment.

data.title: Anthropic's IPO Success Shifts Spotlight to OpenAI — WSJ
data.description:
By Berber Jin and Corrie Driebusch

Anthropic's successful debut shifts the spotlight to its older rival OpenAI, which is preparing to mount a listing of its own.

The ChatGPT maker has already filed confidential IPO documents with the Securities and Exchange Commission, and its CFO Sarah Friar has told staff that the company plans to go public in 2027 or sooner. OpenAI's revenue accelerated in the third quarter, but its operating losses are much larger than Anthropic's.

Anthropic's giant IPO cash haul-and the warm reception it received from public investors-will likely incentivize OpenAI to move more quickly. Both companies need to raise as much money as they can in order to pay for giant computing commitments in coming years

Some advisers say this week's deal also puts OpenAI in the strange position of cheering for Anthropic's success, since Anthropic's stock price and valuation will be used to help price OpenAI's future IPO.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: The Cigna Group Deepens Community Impact Strategy, Adds New Commitment Supporting People with Complex Health Conditions
data.description:
• New three-year strategy includes support for youth mental health, veteran well-being and people living with complex health conditions and pairs grant funding with employee volunteerism to deepen impact
  • Grant funding across three strategic commitments will support nonprofits serving communities in AZ, CT, FL, GA, IL, MO, NJ, PA, TN and TX
  • Applications open now through December 18 for nonprofits supporting patients and caregivers navigating complex health conditions

BLOOMFIELD, Conn., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Cigna Group () is deepening its community impact strategy with a focus on supporting youth mental health, veteran well-being and people living with complex health conditions and their caregivers. The strategy includes a three-year, $31.5 million commitment from The Cigna Group Foundation, the philanthropic arm of The Cigna Group, to support nonprofit organizations aligned to these areas. Informed by research identifying pressing community needs, the funding supports populations and areas where data suggests focused efforts can have a meaningful impact.

Experience the full interactive Multichannel News Release here: https://www.multivu.com/cigna/9433451-en-cigna-group-deepens-community-impact-strategy

Since The Cigna Group unveiled a refreshed approach to community engagement in 2024, the Foundation has invested more than $30 million in nearly 190 nonprofit organizations, with grant-funded projects reaching at least 321,000 people. The evolved strategy builds on that work, pairing grant funding with employee volunteerism, expertise and partnerships to help nonprofit organizations strengthen their impact in the communities they serve.

"Over the past several years, we've seen the tangible impact we can make when we invest in strong nonprofit partners and come together to help communities achieve better health and vitality," said Melissa Skottegaard, board chair of The Cigna Group Foundation. "We're building on what's working, bringing together funding, collaboration and the skills of our employee volunteers to address some of the most pressing health challenges facing communities across the street and around the world."

Three Strategic Commitments Support Health and Well-Being

Beginning in 2027, the Foundation will invest $31.5 million over three years across three strategic commitments addressing critical community needs.

  • Improving Youth Mental Health. Building on its longstanding commitment to youth mental health, the Foundation will invest $10.5 million over three years to continue supporting organizations that expand access to mental health support and resources, with a focus on meeting the growing needs of adolescents ages 12-18.
  • Enhancing Support for Veterans. The Foundation will deepen its support for veterans with a $10.5 million, three-year investment in programs that help veterans achieve greater stability through housing, employment and financial well-being initiatives.
  • Supporting Complex Care Patients. A new $10.5 million, three-year Supporting Complex Care Patients grant program will strengthen services for patients and caregivers, with initial grantmaking focused on autoimmune and inflammatory conditions, blood disorders, cancer, neurological conditions and rare diseases. Funding will help address non-clinical barriers to treatment, including care navigation, education, peer support, mental health resources and assistance with essential social needs.

"For people living with complex health conditions, managing their health requires ongoing clinical management, specialized treatment and coordination across multiple providers, treatments and support systems," said Dr. Amy Flaster, chief medical officer, The Cigna Group and board member, The Cigna Group Foundation. "I see firsthand how their needs can extend beyond medical treatment, whether it's understanding care options, finding emotional and peer support, or addressing practical needs that can make it harder to manage their health day to day."

"Community organizations can be a powerful source of support for people navigating complex health conditions," said Matt Perlberg, president of Evernorth Pharmacy & Care Delivery, executive vice president of Customer Innovation, and board member of The Cigna Group Foundation. "By helping patients and caregivers connect with resources and overcome barriers to care, these organizations can provide important support alongside essential medical treatment, helping people navigate their health and care journey."

Eligible nonprofit organizations can apply for the Supporting Complex Care Patients grant program through December 18 at 5:00 p.m. ET.

Funding Opportunities Across 10 States

Through its three strategic commitments, The Cigna Group Foundation will provide funding opportunities for nonprofit organizations serving communities in Arizona, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Missouri, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Tennessee and Texas.

Eligible nonprofit organizations may apply for two-year grants of $250,000 within the Foundation's three strategic commitment areas and defined grant program time periods, expanding community-based programs and services that help connect people with support services, overcome barriers and improve long-term health and well-being.

The Foundation will also continue supporting current grantees, including nonprofits supported through its Health Equity Impact Fund in Hartford, Connecticut, Memphis, Tennessee and St. Louis, Missouri.

Continuing National Partnership To Improve Youth Mental Health

The Cigna Group Foundation will continue its national partnership with Boys & Girls Clubs of America, building on a shared commitment to improving youth mental health and well-being, now with a greater focus on supporting adolescents.

Since 2024, the partnership has helped expand trauma-informed training efforts to more than 90% of Clubs nationwide, reaching more than 11,000 staff members, while supporting new mental health resources now available at nearly 3,500 Club sites across the country. More than 1,600 young people have been reached through The Cigna Group employee volunteer activities, and employees have contributed more than 2,000 volunteer hours in support of local Clubs.

The partnership will continue to expand access to mental health resources, strengthen volunteer engagement with local Clubs and support the well-being of young people nationwide.

Employee Volunteerism Extends Community Impact

The Cigna Group's community impact strategy pairs financial investments from the Foundation with opportunities for employees to contribute their time and expertise through hands-on and skills-based volunteerism. Together, these efforts help nonprofit partners strengthen their organizations and extend the impact of the Foundation's investments beyond grant funding.

About The Cigna Group

The Cigna Group () is a global health company committed to creating a better future built on the vitality of every individual and every community. We relentlessly challenge ourselves to partner and innovate solutions for better health. The Cigna Group includes products and services marketed under Cigna Healthcare, Evernorth Health Services or its subsidiaries. The Cigna Group maintains sales capabilities in more than 30 countries and jurisdictions and has more than 180 million customer relationships around the world. Learn more at thecignagroup.com.

About The Cigna Group Foundation

The Cigna Group Foundation is a private foundation funded by contributions from The Cigna Group () and its subsidiaries. The Cigna Group Foundation aims to support, collaborate and convene with nonprofit organizations addressing society's greatest health challenges. In addition to increasing access to programs and care in geographies demonstrating significant need, the Foundation responds with humanitarian aid relief during critical times and strengthens colleagues' support of causes through matching donations and volunteer rewards. To learn more, visit www.thecignagroup.com/community.

Media contact:

data.title: ExpreS2ion Announces Restructuring to Reduce Costs and Prioritise ES2B-C001
data.description:
Hørsholm, Denmark, 19 November 2026 – ExpreS2ion Biotech Holding AB (publ) (“ExpreS2ion” or the “Company”) today announces that its Board of Directors has resolved to implement a restructuring, including a reduction in workforce, to lower operating costs and prioritise the development and partnering of ES2B-C001, its lead HER2-targeted active immunotherapy. The number of employees will be reduced from 21 to five during 2027 and, once fully implemented in the second half of 2027, the restructuring is expected to reduce annual operating costs by approximately SEK 30 million. The restructuring does not by itself finance operations beyond the Phase I primary readout, and the Board is evaluating financing alternatives. The Company maintains its planned translational study readout before year-end 2026 and primary readout from the Phase I five-dose priming phase in Q1 2027. Phase II initiation remains targeted for the second half of 2027, subject to financing and partnering, Phase I data, regulatory interactions and final protocol development. Furthermore, Board member Karin Garre has decided to step down from the Board at the end of the year.

Restructuring and financial impact

The restructuring is intended to substantially reduce the Company’s ongoing cash requirements. Compared with the Company’s previous plan, operating costs are expected to be reduced by approximately SEK 23 million in 2027, as the measures take effect during the year, and by approximately SEK 30 million on an annual basis from 2028, once fully implemented. For comparison, operating costs amounted to SEK 56.5 million for the full year 2025 and SEK 57.4 million for the first nine months of 2026. Restructuring costs, mainly pay during notice periods and severance, are estimated at up to approximately SEK 5 million and are expected to be charged largely to the fourth quarter of 2026.

Cash and cash equivalents amounted to SEK 35.8 million on 31 October 2026, before settlement of existing liabilities. The restructuring does not by itself finance the Company’s operations beyond the Phase I primary readout. The Board is evaluating financing alternatives to fund ongoing working capital needs and the partnering process that follows the readout. However, there is no guarantee that such financing can be obtained on acceptable terms for the Company. The measures do not remove the need for additional financing and partnering to initiate Phase II.

ES2B-C001 progress and next milestones

As reported in October 2026, all 19 patients have been enrolled and started treatment in the Phase I trial in advanced HER2-positive or HER2-low breast cancer. At the 5 October 2026 data cut-off, anti-HER2 antibody responses had been observed in 12 of 13 evaluable patients. No dose-limiting toxicities or serious adverse events assessed as related to ES2B-C001 had been reported. These observations are preliminary and do not establish clinical benefit.

  • Translational studies: results from three studies of patient sera, expected December 2026, will show whether the antibody response is polyclonal, engages Fc-mediated immune functions and inhibits HER2-positive tumour cell growth in laboratory assays, giving insight into the response’s mechanism of action and supporting development and partnering discussions.
  • Phase I primary readout: the last patient’s last visit in the five-dose priming phase is expected at the end of December 2026, followed by announcement of the primary readout in Q1 2027. Eligible patients may continue into the maintenance phase.
  • Phase II: initiation remains targeted for the second half of 2027, subject to financing and partnering, Phase I data, regulatory interactions and final protocol development. Planning focuses on evaluating ES2B-C001 alongside standard of care in a first-line treatment setting, informed by Scientific Advisory Board input.

ExpreS2ion continues active business development discussions to support further development of ES2B-C001. Alongside this priority, the Company is seeking to preserve the value of its partnered programmes and ExpreS2™ platform while reducing the resources committed to other activities.

Partnered programmes and allocation of resources

The restructuring will focus internal resources on ES2B-C001 while maintaining the value from work that is largely completed and can be supported by remaining staff. The approach to other programmes reflects their funding, contractual obligations and scope for further development by partners.

  • Malaria: ExpreS2 supports the Oxford-led RH5.1, R78C, RH5.2-VLP and Pfs48/45 vaccine programmes. RH5.1 and R78C are covered by the licensing agreement with Serum Institute of India announced in November 2025, providing a route to further development, manufacturing and commercialisation, with potential milestone and royalty income for ExpreS2ion. These partner-led programmes remain an important application of the platform. The Company will prioritise its contractual commitments while pursuing opportunities to realise value from its malaria-related activities.
  • Influenza: The INDIGO consortium concluded in Q1 2026, and ExpreS2ion does not plan further work without new external funding. As part of the restructuring, the Company’s participation in MucoVax, the approximately 67% Innovation Fund Denmark-funded preclinical mucosal influenza vaccine collaboration, will be discussed directly with its partners in the collaboration, including any required handover and outstanding grant obligations.
  • Nipah: The EU-funded VICI-Disease consortium is developing a Nipah virus vaccine towards initial clinical evaluation. ExpreS2ion’s contribution has focused on antigen development using ExpreS2 and support for transfer to manufacturing. Next consortium steps include the completion of manufacturing and preclinical safety work and the required regulatory approvals, with clinical initiation targeted during 2027. The programme supports pandemic preparedness; future commercial opportunities remain dependent on further development and procurement arrangements.

ExpreS2 platform and contract services

ExpreS2ion is pursuing strategic partnerships for its ExpreS2 platform and related contract services activities, with the aim of preserving their commercial value while reducing the Company’s internal cost base. The proprietary Drosophila S2 expression system has been used to express more than 500 proteins and supports complex antigen production, scalable manufacturing processes and selected glycosylation modifications. ExpreS2-produced antigens have been used in clinical programmes through Phase III, providing a track record relevant to potential development and manufacturing partners.

ExpreS2ion will no longer prioritise expansion of its standalone CRO services business and will adapt its capacity to the smaller organisation. Internal platform and service activities will be aligned with ES2B-C001 requirements, the capacity of the smaller organisation and existing contractual obligations. The Company continues to pursue strategic partnerships for the ExpreS2 platform and related activities; the outcome and timing of these discussions remain uncertain.

Management and Board

Following the restructuring, the management team will remain unchanged. CEO Bent U. Frandsen, CSO Max Søgaard and CFO Keith Alexander will lead the focused organisation. Furthermore, Board member Karin Garre has decided this presents a good moment to step down from the Board at the end of the year, as part of reducing her professional commitments. Following Karin Garre’s departure from the Board, the Board will consist of Martin R. Jensen, Michel Baijot and Jakob Knudsen.

Board Chair Martin R. Jensen comments:

“Reducing our workforce is a difficult decision, and I want to acknowledge the contribution, commitment and talent of the employees who are leaving. ES2B-C001 has completed enrolment of all 19 patients in Phase I, and our priorities are clear: report the translational results and the Phase I primary readout, and use that evidence to advance development and partnering discussions. A lower cost base, with the leadership team remaining in place, will help us focus our resources on these priorities while we pursue the financing and partnerships needed for Phase II. I would also like to thank Karin Garre for her commitment and very significant contribution to the Board over the years.”

CEO Bent U. Frandsen comments:

“I fully support the Board’s hard decision, but it means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who, building on more than 15 years of proprietary research, developed the ExpreS2 platform, which has been validated in a Phase III trial. This decision is about where we focus our resources, not the quality of their work, and I want to thank each of them. With preliminary antibody responses in 12 of 13 evaluable patients and no dose-limiting toxicities, our focus is now on the Phase I readout and on finding the right partner to take ES2B-C001 into Phase II.”

About ExpreS2ion

ExpreS2ion is a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing ES2B-C001, its lead active immunotherapy targeting HER2-expressing cancers, currently in Phase I clinical development. ES2B-C001 is built on the Company’s proprietary ExpreS2™ protein expression platform, which also supports partnered vaccine programmes in infectious diseases. Proteins produced using ExpreS2 have progressed through clinical development, including Phase III. The Company pursues development, licensing and strategic partnering opportunities across its lead asset, platform and partnered programmes. ExpreS2ion Biotech Holding AB is listed on Nasdaq First North Growth Market. For additional information, please visit www.expres2ionbio.com.

data.title: Biohaven rises after early-stage trial data for cancer therapy
data.description:
Biohaven shares rose on Thursday after the company announced early-stage trial data for its cancer candidate BHV-1530 and disclosed its plans to advance the antibody-drug conjugate in a pivotal trial as early as next year.

Based on an Oct. 19 data cut from a Phase 1 trial, the Connecticut-based biotech said that nine out of 10 efficacy-evaluable patients with activating FGFR3 alterations achieved a tumor reduction, while six with UC and HPV-positive HNSCC showed a partial response.

All responders were undergoing BHV-1530 therapy as of the data cutoff, including several individuals for more than six months. The ongoing trial was designed to evaluate the FGFR3-directed ADC as a single agent and in combination with an anti-PD-1 antibody in adults with advanced solid tumors such as urothelial cancer.

Based on 30 safety-evaluable patients, the company added that there were no dose-limiting toxicities, treatment-related serious adverse events, or treatment-related deaths.

Having completed a Type C meeting with the FDA in Q4, Biohaven said it expects to begin a pivotal study for BHV-1530 in FGFR3-altered tumors in H1 2027, starting with UC, seeking a potential accelerated approval.

data.description: Canadian grocer Metro's post-strike recovery in fiscal 2027 take time rather than come on immediately, says RBC's Irene Nattel. data.title: Gold hits 14-month low as strong dollar, rate bets weigh
data.description:
Key points:
  • Bullion touched its lowest level since Sept 2025 in the session
  • Markets see 94% chance of a 25-bp rate hike next month
  • Recent computer outages, AI worries could lead investors to 'hard assets' like gold, analyst says

By Anjana Anil

Gold fell more than 1% to a 14-month low on Thursday, as it continued to face pressure from dollar strength, with markets fully pricing in a rate hike at the Federal Reserve's December meeting owing to stubborn inflation.

Spot gold was down 1.3% at $3,674.13 per ounce by 2:05 p.m. ET (1905 GMT), after touching its lowest level since September 2025 at $3,667.19 earlier in the session.

US gold futures for December delivery settled 1.5% lower at $3,685.50.

"Interest rate expectations and a strong dollar are two factors weighing on gold prices today. Minutes from last month's FOMC meeting showed almost all Fed officials expected interest rates will need to move higher, and inflation data released since that meeting support further rate increases here in the US," said Chris Gaffney, head of World Markets at EverBank.

The dollar index this week reached its highest level since April 2025, making greenback-priced gold more expensive for overseas buyers.

Fed minutes released showed policymakers saw rising inflation risks that may warrant a stronger policy response, reinforcing sentiments already expressed by several policymakers throughout the week, including Governor Christopher Waller who said the Fed may need to respond more aggressively to rising prices.

Fed Governor Michael Barr said he would likely support tighter monetary policy in an economy still facing inflation pressures.

"We're seeing some selling pressure in the stock market that has maybe prompted some margin calls, selling pressure in the metals markets. It's a rough situation in the gold and silver markets at present," said Jim Wyckoff, a market analyst at American Gold Exchange.

Traders see a 94% chance of a 25-basis-point rate increase in December and a 6% probability of a 50-bp hike <FedWatch>.

Higher rates reduce the appeal of non-yielding bullion.

Markets would need to see increased demand for gold from both consumers and central banks for prices to recover, Gaffney said, adding, "recent computer outages, and worries about AI could lead investors to turn back toward 'hard assets' such as gold."

Spot silver fell 1.5% to $44.34 per ounce, platinum lost 0.7% to $1,361.18, and palladium shed 3% to $919.14.
